papers.title: Quantum State Discrimination Enhanced by FPGA-Based AI Engine Technology
papers.abstract: Identifying the state of a quantum bit (qubit), known as quantum state discrimination, is a crucial operation in quantum computing. However, it has been the most error-prone and time-consuming operation on superconducting quantum processors. Due to stringent timing constraints and algorithmic complexity, most qubit state discrimination methods are executed offline. In this work, we present an enhanced real-time quantum state discrimination system leveraging FPGA-based AI Engine technology. A multi-layer neural network has been developed and implemented on the AMD Xilinx VCK190 FPGA platform, enabling accurate in-situ state discrimination and supporting mid-circuit measurement experiments for multiple qubits. Our approach leverages recent advancements in architecture research and design, utilizing specialized AI/ML accelerators to optimize quantum experiments and reduce the use of FPGA resources.

similar_to.title: Developments in superconducting erasure qubits for hardware-efficient quantum error correction

summary.summary: This work presents a real-time quantum state discrimination system using a multi-layer neural network implemented on the AMD Xilinx VCK190 FPGA AI Engine to classify qubit IQ-plane readout data. The approach achieves $81.6$ ns kernel latency with $0.25\%$ resource utilization on the AI Engine tile array, enabling mid-circuit measurements while preserving FPGA programmable logic resources for other quantum control tasks.
summary.motivation: Quantum state discrimination is the bottleneck in superconducting qubit readout and mid-circuit measurements, requiring sub-microsecond latency and high classification fidelity. Traditional FPGA programmable logic implementations consume scarce resources even for 8–16 qubit systems, prompting exploration of specialized AI accelerators to offload this compute-intensive task.
summary.method: A three-layer ReLU neural network with vector operations mapped onto the AI Engine's 400-tile array of 7-way VLIW processors, fed by a streaming pipeline from DDR4 memory via AXI Stream interfaces, operating at $1250$ MHz on the Versal AI platform.
summary.result: Kernel latency of $81.6$ ns (versus $54$ ns for prior RFSoC-based QubiCML), occupying only $0.25\%$ of kernel tiles, $0.50\%$ of buffer tiles, and $0.44\%$ of stream interconnect tiles, with estimated power consumption of $0.593$ W dominated by on-chip memory activity ($0.501$ W).
